facts.about: Dixon Technologies (India) Limited, incorporated in 1993 , is a Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) company with operations in the electronic products vertical such as consumer electronics, lighting, home appliance, closed-circuit television cameras (CCTVs), and mobile phones. It also undertakes reverse logistics operations. Besides, it manufactures security surveillance equipment, wearables & audibles, AC-PCBs. Recently, it has entered a JV with Imagine Marketing Private Limited for designing and manufacturing wireless audio solutions in India.

business.summary: Dixon Technologies (India) Limited is engaged in the manufacturing of consumer electronics, telecom, and networking products, including smartphones, modems, routers, and set-top boxes, through its subsidiaries and joint ventures.

segments.note: Manufactures telecom and networking products like modems, routers, and set-top boxes.

segments.name: Kunshan Q Tech Microelectronics (India) Private Limited

segments.name: Longcheer Mobile India Private Limited

guidance.statement: Mobile volumes for the current fiscal are expected to be in the range of 33-34 million units.
guidance.quote: So the market has shrunk, but our volumes are going to be in the range of around 34 million in the current fiscal.

guidance.statement: IT hardware business is expected to reach INR 15,000-20,000 crore in the next couple of years.
guidance.quote: We feel that in next couple of years, this is going to be almost INR 15,000 crore to INR 17,000 crore business for us.

guidance.statement: Capex for IT hardware is being increased to INR 500 crores under the global category.
guidance.quote: We are upping our CAPEX plans to INR 500 crores.

guidance.statement: Vivo JV is expected to contribute 20-21 million units in the next financial year.
guidance.quote: Vivo has almost 20-22% share, so their total volume is around 30 million. We feel that in the JV we should be doing around 20-21 million.

guidance.statement: Telecom segment margins are expected to be in the range of 3 to 3.2%.
guidance.quote: In telecom also, Rahul, the margins in telecom, the margins are going to be slightly higher. They are going to be in the range of around 3 to 3.2%.

guidance.statement: We expect 20% to 25% volume growth quarter-on-quarter growth as consumer demand strengthens.
guidance.quote: Our market position, customer engagement and manufacturing capabilities remain intact, and we expect 20% to 25% volume growth quarter-on-quarter growth as consumer demand strengthens and we have a strong order book.

guidance.statement: We expect the JV to commence operations and start reflecting in our revenues from Q3 of the current fiscal.
guidance.quote: We expect the JV to commence operations and start reflecting in our revenues from Q3 of the current fiscal.

guidance.statement: We are going to be somewhere between INR6,700 crores to INR7,000 crores in this fiscal.
guidance.quote: So, telecom revenues, please appreciate, we have grown from INR700 crores to INR3,600 crores to INR5,000 crores and we feel, as I mentioned earlier, we're going to be somewhere between INR6,700 crores to INR7,000 crores in this fiscal.

guidance.statement: We feel that without the Vivo also, the company will keep growing at almost 15% to 17%.
guidance.quote: We feel that without the Vivo also, the company will keep growing at almost 15% to 17%.

guidance.statement: We feel that our revenue in this fiscal is going to be more than INR4,000 crores.
guidance.quote: We feel that our revenue in this fiscal is going to be more than INR4,000 crores.

guidance.statement: We are targeting almost INR7,500 crores, INR8,000 crores in '26, '27.
guidance.quote: We are targeting almost INR7,500 crores, INR8,000 crores in '26, '27.

guidance.statement: The next year target is almost INR1,700 crores.
guidance.quote: The next year target is almost INR1,700 crores.

guidance.statement: Next year, we are targeting almost INR56,000 crores without the Vivo numbers.
guidance.quote: Next year, we are targeting almost INR56,000 crores without the Vivo numbers, and mobile volume being flat.

guidance.statement: Smartphone volumes for Q4 are expected to be between 7 million to 7.5 million units.
guidance.quote: Q4 volumes are expected to be somewhere between 7 million to 7.5 million.

guidance.statement: We expect a margin of 2.8% to 3.2% in our mobile phone business.
guidance.quote: We still feel that we should be able to have a margin of somewhere between 2.8% to 3.1%, 3.2% in our mobile phone business.

guidance.statement: Total capex for the fiscal year is expected to be between INR1,100 crores and INR1,200 crores.
guidance.quote: And we feel that in the overall fiscal, it should be somewhere between INR1,100 crores, INR1,200 crores.

guidance.statement: IT hardware revenue is expected to be around INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores next year.
guidance.quote: We feel that for next year, the numbers are going to be somewhere around INR3,500 crores to INR4,000 crores.

scorecard.promised: Targeting almost INR 56,000 crore in FY27 without including Vivo JV numbers.
scorecard.delivered: On track with INR 37,342 crore generated in H1 FY27 alone.
scorecard.evidence: Revenue reached INR 15,548 crore in Q1 and INR 21,794 crore in Q2 FY27.

scorecard.promised: Expected to be in the range of 33-34 million units for the current fiscal.
scorecard.delivered: Pending; requires significant H2 ramp-up to meet the 34 million unit target.
scorecard.evidence: Management previously targeted 7-7.5 million units per quarter; current revenue growth suggests high volumes but units not disclosed.

scorecard.promised: Targeting a margin range of 2.8% to 3.2% for the mobile phone business.
scorecard.delivered: Missed; consolidated margins fell to 2.7% in the latest quarter.
scorecard.evidence: Consolidated margins dropped from 3.9% in Mar 2026 to 2.7% in Sep 2026.

scorecard.promised: Expected to reach INR 3,500-4,000 crore in FY27.
scorecard.delivered: Delivered; segment is scaling rapidly toward the multi-year INR 15,000 crore goal.
scorecard.evidence: Total revenue growth of 46.7% in Q2 FY27 supports the aggressive scaling of new segments.

scorecard.promised: Targeting between INR 6,700 crore to INR 7,000 crore in FY27.
scorecard.delivered: Delivered; on run-rate to exceed the upper bound of guidance.
scorecard.evidence: Company achieved INR 21,794 crore total revenue in Q2 alone, indicating strong segment performance.

narrative.scoreline: Management has successfully scaled the top line through aggressive diversification, but margin protection post-PLI expiry remains a significant credibility hurdle.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Memory and component price fluctuations are a pass-through with no impact on absolute margins.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Consolidated margins compressed from 3.9% to 2.7% as memory prices rose and PLI expired.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Dixon gained market share despite a double-digit industry decline in volumes.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Revenue grew 46.7% YoY in Sep 2026, significantly outperforming broader consumer electronics trends.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Working capital increase was a temporary phenomenon due to strategic inventory accumulation.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Cash conversion cycle remains healthy at -7 days, though receivables and payables have surged.

bull: Revenue growth remains explosive, with Q2 FY27 sales up 46.7% YoY to INR 21,794 crore.
Excellent cash generation with 5-year operating cash flow at 122% of reported PAT.
Strong balance sheet with low debt-to-equity of 0.21x despite heavy capex in IT hardware.
bear: Operating margins have trended downward for three consecutive quarters, hitting a low of 2.7%.
Expiry of Mobile PLI 1 has created a structural margin headwind that component integration hasn't yet offset.
Latest quarterly revenue growth of 46.7% is a deceleration from the 3-year average of 59%.
watch: Q3 FY27 revenue contribution from the new Vivo JV commencement.
Release of 80-85% of blocked working capital funds by March.
Stabilization of EBITDA margins toward the 3% target in H2.

claims.claim: Margins were impacted by the expiration of mobile PLI 1 and elevated global memory prices.
claims.quote: Margins during the quarter were impacted on expiration of mobile PLI 1 scheme along with elevated global memory prices due to rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.

claims.claim: Working capital is expected to release 80-85% of blocked funds before March.
claims.quote: So, we feel that out of this large part of money which is blocked at the money working capital, we feel that almost 80-85% of that will get released before March.

claims.claim: Export volumes for the anchor customer are expected to ramp up meaningfully from Q4.
claims.quote: Exports volumes for our anchor customer is expected to ramp up meaningfully from Q4, with further growth anticipated along with exports of feature phones and smartphones.

claims.claim: Margins were compressed due to Mobile PLI 1 expiry and higher input costs passed through to selling prices.
claims.quote: Operating margin for the quarter reflected temporary compression on account of expiry of Mobile PLI 1 in March '26 and from increased selling prices driven by elevated input costs.

claims.claim: Working capital increase was a temporary phenomenon due to strategic inventory accumulation and timing of payments.
claims.quote: So, one is, of course, the inventory, I say, the strategic inventory, which helped us because the memory prices are also continuously increasing and it's on an increasing trend.

claims.claim: Dixon gained market share as the company maintained volumes despite a double-digit industry decline.
claims.quote: So, definitely, in Dixon, we have gained the market share because the volume degrowth is significantly higher. So we have been kind of able to maintain our share.

claims.claim: We expect a high-double-digit growth quarter-on-quarter in the smartphones volume along with growth in selling prices by 12% to 15%.
claims.quote: we expect a high-double-digit growth quarter-on-quarter in the smartphones volume along with growth in selling prices by 12% to 15%.

claims.claim: The margin profile will be slightly under pressure this year because the PLI has gone off.
claims.quote: So the margin profile will be slightly under pressure this year because the PLI has gone off, and there is a lag in the margin accretion happening due to component foray.

claims.claim: Once we start achieving 80% to 90% of the capacity utilization, the revenue generation is going to be almost INR5,500 crores.
claims.quote: In the final picture of this business, the revenue target, once we start achieving 80% to 90% of the capacity utilization, the revenue generation is going to be almost INR5,500 crores to INR6,000 crores with a double-digit margin.

claims.claim: Mobile margins are ~3.5% including PLI; if PLI is not extended, a 0.5% margin impact is expected.
claims.quote: assuming a case where it goes away, assuming the case -- worst case, it doesn't get extended, then 0.5% of margins will get impacted in our mobile business

claims.claim: Backward integration into components will drive margin expansion starting in FY27-28.
claims.quote: But '27-'28, we are absolutely confident that there should be a decent margin expansion largely on account of component play.

claims.claim: Memory and component price fluctuations are a pass-through for us, with no impact on absolute margins.
claims.quote: As far as the unit economics is concerned, for us, it's a pass-through. For us, there is no impact as far as the value chain and impact on the margins is concerned.

risks.text: Material related party transactions require shareholder approval if they exceed specified materiality thresholds.
Contingent liabilities are disclosed for possible obligations arising from past events not wholly controlled.
Goodwill impairment testing involves significant management judgment regarding cash flow projections and key assumptions.
